Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (US, Japan, Australia, Germany, France, UK, Singapore primary lens)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    A global bond selloff is deepening across major economies, driven by Middle East conflict-fueled energy price spikes, persistent inflation above central bank targets, and mounting sovereign debt concerns. US 10-year Treasury yields are approaching 4.81%, with 5% flagged as the next critical threshold. Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish commentary has amplified rate-hike expectations. Corporate bond issuance from AI-sector hyperscalers is adding supply pressure. Bond vigilante dynamics are resurfacing, with fiscal credibility being stress-tested across the US, Japan, UK, France, and Germany. Policy response options being floated include Treasury buybacks, YCC, and QE — the latter seen as bullish for gold.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (US yields and rate trajectory are the central anchor of the article, with global spillovers framed relative to the US)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly centered on rising yield dynamics and rate-hike pricing)
Probability of increase: 68% (explicitly stated in article — traders pricing ~68% chance of a US rate hike the following week)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (holding is not a theme; no meaningful discussion of a pause scenario)
Probability of holding: 32% (residual, implied by the 68% hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (cuts are entirely absent from the narrative; the direction is unambiguously upward)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (Distinctly hawkish — Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish remarks, 68% hike probability priced in, 10Y approaching 5%, 2Y at multi-year highs, Brent crude adding fresh inflation pressure, and no dovish counterweight present in the article)
